title: Effects of digit code
statement: Let $c$ be a memory address distinct from the address holding the constant $1$, and let $L$ be a list of binary digits, each less than $2$. If the initial memory holds the word value $1$ at the constant-one address, executing the digit code for $L$ at address $c$ leaves the natural number represented by those digits at $c$. It leaves memory unchanged outside $\{c\}$.
hypotheses_covered: Every digit in $L$ is less than $2$
Initial memory at the constant-one address encodes $1$
